title: Routing of Earnings and Credits Among a Host's Payout Methods
content:
Earnings of a stay are released to the Payout Methods method whose routed listing is the stay's listing, when such a method is active and its rail allows listing routing; otherwise to the default method. A method that is not active receives no release; its share goes to the default method instead.

## Terms

1. **Stay earnings.** Released to the method routed to the stay's listing when that method is active and its rail allows listing routing; in every other case, released to the default method.
2. **Credits.** Protection reimbursements, guest damage payments, penalty waivers and premium refunds are credited to the default method, as the rail's claim-credit routing provides.
3. **Changing the default.** Setting a new default clears the default flag on the old method and stamps the moment the new method became the default. Transfers to a newly set default are held under the default-change security hold.
4. **Removing the default.** The default method can be removed only when the host has at least the number of active methods the rail sets for removal of a default (2 on every rail), and another active method must be made the default first.
5. **Removed balance.** A removed method's undisbursed balance moves to the default method.
6. **Inactive methods.** A method that is not active receives no release; its share goes to the default method instead.

## Release destination table

| Is there a method routed to the stay's listing? | Is that method active? | Does its rail allow listing routing? | Earnings released to |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | The routed method |
| Yes | Yes | No | The default method |
| Yes | No (pending verification or on hold) | Either | The default method |
| No | — | — | The default method |

## Hypothetical cases

- An imagined host routes one listing to an active PayPal method and keeps an active Direct Deposit (ACH) method as default. A stay at that listing releases to the PayPal method; a stay at any other listing releases to the ACH method.
- The same PayPal method is placed on hold. A later stay at the routed listing releases to the default ACH method, because a method that is not active receives no release.
- An imagined host routes a listing to a Western Union Cash Pickup method. That rail does not allow listing routing, so the listing's stays release to the default method.
- An imagined host holds 2 active methods and wishes to remove the default one. The other active method must first be made the default; the removed method's undisbursed balance then moves to that new default.
